title: Nike Tuned Air Unlocks a New Era of Precision Cushioning for Athletes Across Sports
summary: NIKE, Inc. is introducing a breakthrough method of make that’s changing how the company creates Air, building on a legacy of athlete-centered innovation to provide unprecedented control over how Air looks, feels and performs.
body_markdown:
NIKE, Inc. is introducing a breakthrough method of make that’s[changing how the company creates Air](https://about.nike.com/en/magazine/how-nike-made-tuned-air) , building on a legacy of[athlete-centered innovation](https://about.nike.com/en/newsroom/releases/nike-inc-unveils-the-next-generation-of-innovation-across-performance-sports-and-sportswear) to provide unprecedented control over how Air looks, feels and performs.


Tuned Air leverages a proprietary digital print and selective lamination process to create distinct cushioning, comfort, durability and responsiveness for different athletes across sports.


Simply put: The innovation unlocks new possibilities for Air and its benefits underfoot.


Nike Air has long been the ultimate advantage for athletes. For nearly 50 years, it has delivered lightweight, resilient cushioning that holds up mile after mile and season after season. Few platforms can be adapted across such a wide range of qualities, from the responsiveness of Zoom Air to the comfort of Air Max. The technology has even made its way into apparel. What began as an unconventional idea, putting air inside a shoe, has broadened into a genealogy, with each Air unit containing its own look, feel and set of performance attributes.


“Our biggest breakthroughs don’t stay in one product. They become platforms that serve athletes in more ways,” says Phil McCartney, EVP, Chief Innovation, Design & Product Officer. “Tuned Air gives us greater speed and precision in how we create Air, so we can design the right cushioning experience around the needs of each athlete and sport.”


Tuned Air was born from the same question that turned Nike Air from a lofty concept into a reality: What if underfoot cushioning could be creatively reimagined from the inside out?


The inside of the Air unit held the secret. If engineers could remove the need for pins and rigid zones that traditionally give Air units their shape, they could better optimize how Air compresses and responds underfoot. By liberating these internal structures, athletes could benefit from purer, less restricted Air units.


Some of Nike’s most radical innovations were inspired by creations both ordinary (a waffle iron, an ice cube tray) and awe-inspiring (sports cars, the Pompidou). The inspiration for Tuned Air came from another unexpected place outside of the industry: the glossy, vibrant colors on magazine covers. Refined over a decade, Nike engineers and scientists considered how digital inks, applied inside the Air unit, could give it incredibly precise yet variable cushioning features.


The Tuned Air platform takes this proprietary digital ink and combines it with a selective lamination process that prevents bonding between the Air unit and its internal core. Everywhere there is ink in the core, the core will not bond to the unit. Everywhere there is not ink, it will bond. A near unlimited combination of shapes, geometries and visual treatments is possible through this specialized process.


As a result, all aspects of Air construction have been turned upside-down. Nike engineers are no longer constrained mechanically by the height of the Air unit, removing a longstanding challenge in Air unit manufacturing and allowing Nike to create more nuanced cushioning systems for athletes.


Then there’s the factor of speed. Tuned Air doesn't just change how Nike makes Air. It changes how quickly Nike can develop it, from concept to final unit.


At Nike’s[Advanced Product Creation Center](https://about.nike.com/en/magazine/nike-spaces-sports-design-innovation-performance) , the average development time for new Air units has dropped by 70%. Prototypes that once took three weeks can now be made in three days. By removing traditional manufacturing constraints and accelerating the process from design through testing, Nike can move from athlete insight to prototype to performance solution faster than ever before. This speed creates more opportunities to experiment, learn from athletes and refine new solutions, ultimately bringing more possibilities to the Air platform.


“The possibilities with Tuned Air are endless,” says McCartney. “We can move from athlete insight to new Air solutions faster, create them with greater precision for different sports and deliver that experience more consistently across sizes. Tuned Air gives us a new way to create Air at scale, bringing the benefits of Air to more athletes in more ways.”


Tuned Air will be available for runners in late 2027, marking the beginning of a broader platform across sport and Sportswear.
